classification.difficultyReason: Match vertices using marked sides and angles despite changed orientations, select the relevant congruence test, and transfer corresponding values. The right-triangle part adds a routine Pythagorean calculation before identifying the matching base.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals in each.

spec.description: Two horizontally paired triangles with vertex labels and matching one-, two- and three-tick sides. Ordinary source blue outlines use house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=PQ, BC=QR, AC=PR; angle A=30 degrees and angle B=100 degrees. Unknown angles at P,Q,R are alpha,beta,gamma respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown symbols appear.

answer.worked:
$\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PQR$ (SSS), so matching angles are equal.

$\alpha=30^{\circ}$ and $\beta=100^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}\gamma&=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}-100^{\circ}\\\gamma&=50^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontally paired, differently oriented triangles. Retains all vertex labels, side ticks and the matching arcs at A and W.
spec.mathematics: AB=UW, AC=WV, angle A=angle W; angle B=40 degrees, angle C=80 degrees; alpha is at U and beta is at V.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown alpha and beta remain symbolic.

answer.worked:
$AB=UW$, $AC=WV$ and $\angle BAC=\angle UWV$ (marked).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle WUV$ (SAS).

Matching angles give $\alpha=\angle B=40^{\circ}$ and $\beta=\angle C=80^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Two horizontally paired right triangles in the same orientation. Retains the redundant 67-degree given on the left.
spec.mathematics: Each triangle has a 5 cm vertical leg and 13 cm hypotenuse; horizontal bases are a cm and b cm. Both lower-left angles are right angles.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem in the left triangle:

$$\begin{align*}a^2&=13^2-5^2\\a^2&=169-25\\a^2&=144\\a&=12\end{align*}$$

The triangles are congruent by RHS: both have a right angle, hypotenuse $13\text{ cm}$ and another side $5\text{ cm}$. Their matching bases are equal, so $b=12$.

Both base lengths are $12\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Paired triangles retain their differing orientations and corresponding angle marks; no vertex names are added.
spec.mathematics: Left sides are 3,4,6 cm. Its top angle is alpha and lower-left angle is arc-marked. Right alpha is lower right, arc-marked angle upper right; their included side is 3 cm. The remaining sides are x cm rising from lower left and y cm along the base.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given lengths and pronumerals are visible.

answer.worked:
The triangles have two pairs of equal angles: the angles labelled $\alpha$ and the arc-marked angles. Their matching $3\text{ cm}$ sides are equal, so the triangles are congruent (AAS).

Matching sides give $x=6$ and $y=4$, so the lengths are $6\text{ cm}$ and $4\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Horizontally paired reflected triangles with horizontal 7 cm upper sides, alpha at opposite upper ends and matching bottom angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: Left remaining sides are 3 cm on the left and 6 cm toward the upper-right alpha vertex. Right corresponding sides are b cm on the right and a cm toward the upper-left alpha vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: The values of a and b are omitted.

answer.worked:
The triangles have equal angles labelled $\alpha$, equal arc-marked angles and matching $7\text{ cm}$ sides. Therefore they are congruent (AAS).

Matching sides give $a=6$ and $b=3$, so the lengths are $6\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$.
